title: Post-Apocalyptic Gallery Curator
description: The user curates a post-apocalyptic exhibition gallery by arranging SheenChairs and DamagedHelmets across a 4x3 grid floor plan. A material budget conservation law limits total placed objects to 8, and each placement or property change can be undone/redone. The user must position, rotate, and scale objects, assign them to named exhibit zones, and toggle spotlight lighting per zone to complete the gallery layout.
prompt: Create a single HTML file using Three.js r170 (via importmap from cdn.jsdelivr.net) that implements a post-apocalyptic gallery curator. Load SheenChair.glb and DamagedHelmet.glb from the shared_assets folder. Scene setup: a 12x9 unit concrete-textured ground plane divided into a 4x3 grid of cells, each cell 3x3 units. Draw subtle grid lines. Use a perspective camera at position (0,14,16) looking at center. Add ambient light intensity 0.3 and one DirectionalLight. Create a left-side HTML panel with: object palette (Chair and Helmet buttons), a material budget counter showing used/8 max, zone name input, undo and redo buttons, a rotation slider (-180 to 180), a scale slider (0.5 to 2.0), and a per-zone spotlight toggle. Interactions (10-14 steps expected): 1) Select an asset type from the palette. 2) Click a grid cell to place a cloned instance there, decrementing the budget. 3) Click a placed object to select it (highlight with yellow emissive). 4) Use the rotation slider to rotate the selected object around Y axis. 5) Use the scale slider to uniformly scale it. 6) Type a zone name and press Enter to assign the selected object to that named zone. 7) Toggle the spotlight button to add or remove a SpotLight above that zone aimed downward. 8) Drag a placed object to another empty cell to reposition it. 9) Press Delete key to remove a selected object, restoring one budget point. 10) Use undo/redo buttons to reverse or replay any action. Conservation law: total placed objects must never exceed 8. Every action (place, move, delete, rotate, scale, zone assign, spotlight toggle) is pushed onto an undo stack. Redo stack clears on new action. Store each action as a command object with execute and undo methods. Use OrbitControls for camera. Raycasting for cell and object selection. Display a status bar at the bottom showing the last action performed. All UI uses clean dark-themed HTML/CSS overlays.
